docs.title: PFI Documentation
docs.text: PFI (Probability Flow Inference) provides estimators to learn a score model and a probability-flow model from time-resolved cross-sectional data. The package is organized around a high-level composite estimator API, and a lower-level API for users who want to control the score stage, the flow stage, or the model classes directly.

docs.title: Package structure
docs.text: Module Content pfi make_pfi_estimator and the composite PFI estimator (score stage, then flow stage). pfi.score ScoreEstimator; score models in pfi.score.models (DSMScore, OUScore); the denoising score matching solver DSM_ in pfi.score.solvers. pfi.flow FlowEstimator; flow and growth models in pfi.flow.models (CLEFlow, MultiplicativeFlow, AdditiveFlow, AutonomousODEFlow, ODEFlow, OUFlow, AutonomousGrowth, ...); interpolants in pfi.flow.interpolants; path ensembles in pfi.flow.paths; solvers in pfi.flow.solvers. pfi.base Model, the base class of every score, flow and growth model, and its mixins (network architecture, input normalization, output perturbation). pfi.utils data loading and conversion (pfi.utils.data), simulators of reference processes (pfi.utils.simulations: toggle switch, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck), and neural-network building blocks (pfi.utils.nns).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:vchz/pfi.git
cd pfi
pip install -e .

Main dependencies include numpy, torch, tqdm, POT, geomloss, torchcubicspline, and scanpy.

docs.title: Data format and loading
docs.text:
All estimators expect a matrix X with shape (n_samples_total, ndim + 1):

  • columns 0..ndim-1: state variables
  • last column: time

If you already have snapshots grouped by time, convert them with X_from_snapshots:

from pfi.utils.data import X_from_snapshots

X = X_from_snapshots(snaps, times)

load_data accepts either:

  • a local .h5ad / .h5ad.gz path
  • the aliases "natcomm" or "kaggle"

For these aliases, the data is fetched from the Zenodo repository associated with the package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19237707. Downloaded files are cached in pfi.utils.data.PFI_DATA_FOLDER, which defaults to ~/pfi_data.

For the exact function signature and outputs, see load_data.

docs.title: Using a composite estimator
docs.text:
The main high-level entry point is make_pfi_estimator. It creates a composite PFI object from a score estimator and a flow estimator. The fitting order is fixed: score first, then flow.

import torch
from pfi import make_pfi_estimator
from pfi.flow.models import CLEFlow
from pfi.score.models import DSMScore

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

score_model = DSMScore(
    sizes=[128, 128, 128, 128],
    batch_norm="zscore",
)

flow_model = CLEFlow(
    score=None,
    sizes=[128, 128, 128],
    lx=1.5,
)

est = make_pfi_estimator(
    score_model=score_model,
    flow_model=flow_model,
    s_solver="dsm",
    f_solver="pfm",
    s_solver_kwargs={"L": 5, "lr": 5e-4, "n_epochs": 4000},
    f_solver_kwargs={"fac": 2, "lr": 1e-3, "n_epochs": 2000},
    device=device,
    random_state=0,
)
est.fit(X)

This is the standard high-level usage pattern. For the complete signature, see make_pfi_estimator. The resulting object is documented in PFI.

docs.title: Quick note on the solvers
docs.text:
The score stage is exposed through ScoreEstimator. The solver currently supported there is:

  • dsm: denoising score matching, taken from: https://doi.org/10.1162/NECO_a_00142, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1907.05600. The noise kernel is Gaussian by default; solver_kwargs={"kernel": "laplace"} uses a Laplace kernel, whose score tends to a constant away from the data instead of growing linearly.

The flow stage is exposed through FlowEstimator. The main solver names are:

  • pfm: the flow-matching solver, please cite: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.25062.
  • pfm-linear: the same procedure, solved in closed form for the linear OUFlow model.
  • upfi: the neural-ODE-style UPFI solver, please cite: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2505.13197, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2420621122.
  • future.ufm_ot, future.ufm_uot: experimental unbalanced flow-matching solvers.
  • external.deepruotv2: wrapper of an external solver, for comparison.

docs.title: Low level usage
docs.text:
If you want finer control, work with the two stages separately using ScoreEstimator and FlowEstimator directly.

By default ScoreEstimator uses DSMScore, but you can provide your own instantiated score model. FlowEstimator accepts an instantiated flow model and an optional growth model.

from pfi.score import ScoreEstimator
from pfi.flow import FlowEstimator
from pfi.flow.models import CLEFlow, AutonomousGrowth

score_est = ScoreEstimator(
    solver="dsm",
    solver_kwargs={"L": 5, "lr": 5e-4, "n_epochs": 4000},
    device=device,
)
score_est.fit(X)

flow_est = FlowEstimator(
    flow=CLEFlow(score=score_est.model_, lx=0.3),
    growth=AutonomousGrowth(),
    solver="pfm",
    solver_kwargs={"fac": 2, "lr": 1e-3, "n_epochs": 2000},
    device=device,
)
flow_est.fit(X)

The score-stage methods are:

  • ScoreEstimator.fit: fit the score model from (x, t) data
  • ScoreEstimator.predict: evaluate the score on time-augmented inputs
  • ScoreEstimator.sample: generate samples at the times present in the input
  • ScoreEstimator.score: compare generated samples to observed samples, time by time

The flow-stage methods are:

  • FlowEstimator.fit: fit the flow model, and optionally a growth model
  • FlowEstimator.predict: evaluate the learned drift
  • FlowEstimator.sample: simulate trajectories from initial states
  • FlowEstimator.score: push source samples to the next later target time and compare them to target samples

docs.title: Trajectories: path ensembles and iterated coupling
docs.text:
Flow matching regresses the model velocity on trajectories through the snapshots. Their construction is set by the paths solver argument, an object from pfi.flow.paths, used like the interp argument for the interpolant:

  • plan-based paths, random paths through the observed cells drawn from transport plans between consecutive snapshots: Independent, ExactOT (the default), Sinkhorn, UnbalancedSinkhorn;
  • map-based paths, a cloud of nodes moved from one snapshot to the next by a transport map: DebiasedSinkhorn (debiased entropic map), and GaussianOT, GaussianDebiasedSinkhorn for Gaussian snapshots.

With n_rounds > 1, the coupling is iterated: every round builds the paths again with the current model's flow as reference dynamics, and retrains the model.

from pfi.flow.interpolants import ChebyshevInterpolant
from pfi.flow.paths import DebiasedSinkhorn

flow_est = FlowEstimator(
    flow=CLEFlow(score=score_est.model_, lx=1.0),
    solver="pfm",
    solver_kwargs={
        "interp": ChebyshevInterpolant(),
        "paths": DebiasedSinkhorn(reg=1.0),
        "n_rounds": 5,
    },
    device=device,
)

For concrete runnable workflows, use the notebooks in the examples folder (https://github.com/vchz/pfi/tree/main/examples):

  • ornstein_uhlenbeck.ipynb: inference of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process;
  • toggle_switch.ipynb: a two-gene toggle switch with growth;
  • interpolants.ipynb: the interpolants on OT trajectories.

For the full public API reference, browse:

  • API reference

docs.title: DebiasedSinkhorn(reg=0.5, stop_thr=None, method='sinkhorn_log', warm_start=True, n_paths=None)
docs.text:
Bases: MapPaths

Debiased Sinkhorn map computed on the node cloud itself.

On interval k, with the pushed nodes q and the cells y of the next snapshot, the entropic plans P_ab: q -> y and P_aa: q -> q (cost |x - y|^2 / 2, regularization reg, uniform weights) give every node its debiased displacement, read on the cloud's own points::

z_i = q_i + sum_j n P_ab[i, j] y_j - sum_m n P_aa[i, m] q_m

The step vanishes when the pushed cloud and the next snapshot have the same law, so the true dynamics is a fixed point of the iterated construction. The Sinkhorn potentials are kept between calls to :meth:fit, to warm-start the next round of an iteration.

Parameters:

  • reg (float, default: 0.5 ) –

    Entropic regularization in data units, on the cost |x - y|^2 / 2. Should be at least a few times the squared nearest-neighbour distance of the snapshots.

  • stop_thr (float or None, default: None ) –

    Sinkhorn marginal tolerance. If None, 1e-8 in float64 and 1e-5 in lower precision (1e-8 is not reachable in float32).

  • method (str, default: 'sinkhorn_log' ) –

    POT backend name.

  • warm_start (bool, default: True ) –

    Start every Sinkhorn solve from the potentials of the previous one.

  • n_paths (int or None, default: None ) –

    Number of paths (see :class:MapPaths).

docs.title: entropic_map_matrix(cov_src, cov_tgt, eps)
docs.text:
Linear part of the entropic barycentric map between two Gaussians.

Entropic plan between N(a, A) and N(b, B) with cost |x - y|^2 / 2 and regularization eps (Janati et al. 2020): E[y | x] = b + K (x - a) with K = C^T A^{-1} and C = A^{1/2} (4 A^{1/2} B A^{1/2} + eps^2 I)^{1/2} A^{-1/2} / 2 - eps I / 2.

docs.title: gaussian_ot_matrix(cov_src, cov_tgt)
docs.text:
Linear part of the OT map from N(., cov_src) to N(., cov_tgt).

T = A^{-1/2} (A^{1/2} B A^{1/2})^{1/2} A^{-1/2}, with A = cov_src and B = cov_tgt; T A T^T = B.

docs.text:
Fit OUFlow in closed form by flow matching on path ensembles.

Every round: (1) the model's flow is the reference dynamics (none in round 1), (2) the paths are built and sampled, (3) they are interpolated at the evaluation times, (4) the score is evaluated there, and (5) B is fitted by exact least squares.

Parameters:

  • dist (list of torch.Tensor) –

    Snapshot list where dist[k] has shape (n_k, ndim).

  • times (torch.Tensor of shape (n_snaps,)) –

    Snapshot times.

  • net (OUFlow) –

    Model, without feature or batch normalization. Its drift matrix net.net_.B is set to the solution.

  • interp (object or None, default: None ) –

    Interpolant implementing fit and predict. If None, ChebyshevInterpolant().

  • paths (PathEnsemble or None, default: None ) –

    Path ensemble. If None, ExactOT().

  • growth_model (None, default: None ) –

    Not supported (must be None).

  • fac (int, default: 4 ) –

    Evaluation times per snapshot (uniform grid over the window, as in PFM_).

  • t_eval (array - like or None, default: None ) –

    Explicit evaluation times (e.g. interval midpoints); overrides fac.

  • ridge (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Ridge penalty ridge * ||B||_F^2 on the time-averaged loss.

  • n_rounds (int, default: 1 ) –

    Rounds of the iterated coupling (1: no iteration).

  • anderson (int, default: 0 ) –

    Anderson memory on B (0: plain iteration).

  • safeguard (bool, default: True ) –

    Keep an Anderson step only if the residual does not grow.

  • tol (float or None, default: None ) –

    Stop when the relative change of B is below tol.

  • push_steps (int, default: 8 ) –

    Runge-Kutta 4 steps per snapshot interval when pushing with the model.

  • history (list or None, default: None ) –

    If a list, receives one dict per round: round, change (relative change of B, NaN for round 1) and B.

  • verbose (bool, default: True ) –

    If True, print one line per round.

  • generator (Generator or None, default: None ) –

    RNG of the path sampling, reset at every round so that all rounds use the same draws (the round map is then deterministic). If None, a generator seeded with 0.

Returns:

  • net ( OUFlow ) –

    Fitted model.

  • growth_model ( None ) –

    Always None.

  • loss_hist ( list of float ) –

    Relative change of B per round (NaN for round 1).

docs.title: clone_module(module)
docs.text:
Clone a torch.nn.Module safely, sharing registered sub-module references.

Standard deepcopy fails when a module contains non-leaf tensors, for example the weight_u / weight_v buffers written by spectral-norm during a forward pass. This function works around the issue by temporarily detaching all registered sub-modules (module._modules) from the module registry, deepcopying only the skeleton (buffers and plain attributes, which are always leaf tensors), and then re-attaching the sub-modules by shared reference on both the original and the clone.

Sharing sub-module references is correct for our use case: the sub-modules attached to a flow model (e.g. a pre-trained score model) are never modified during flow training.

Parameters:

  • module (Module) –

    Module to clone.

Returns:

  • Module –

    Cloned module with the same skeleton and shared sub-module references.

Large-n limit of the closed-form PFM fit (pfm-linear) for an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process.

The exact answer of PFM_LINEAR_ when every snapshot is its exact Gaussian law: the sample averages of the least-squares fit become exact expectations. Nothing is fitted on data; the inputs are the true process and the method (path ensemble, interpolant).

Every round:

  1. reference dynamics: the flow of the current model, v(x, t) = -B x - lx x - D s_t(x) with the exact score s_t(x) = -Sigma_t^{-1} (x - m_t) (none in round 1);
  2. paths: the path ensemble fitted on the exact laws, which returns the exact means and covariances of its nodes (Gaussian ensembles and Independent);
  3. interpolation: the interpolant is linear in the nodes, I(t) = sum_j w_j(t) x_j, so E[I I^T] and E[dI I^T] follow from the node moments;
  4. score: E[s(I) I^T] = -Sigma_t^{-1} (E[I I^T] - m_t E[I]^T);
  5. exact least-squares fit of the drift matrix.

Parameters:

  • B (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Drift and diffusion matrices of the process, dx = -B x dt + sqrt(2 D) dW.

  • D (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Drift and diffusion matrices of the process, dx = -B x dt + sqrt(2 D) dW.

  • m0 (ndarray of shape (ndim,)) –

    Initial mean.

  • S0 (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Initial covariance.

  • times (array-like of shape (K,)) –

    Snapshot times.

  • paths (PathEnsemble) –

    Path ensemble accepting exact laws (GaussianOT, GaussianDebiasedSinkhorn, Independent).

  • interp (object) –

    Interpolant implementing fit and predict (linear in the node values).

  • lx (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Linear degradation coefficient of the model.

  • fac (int, default: 4 ) –

    Evaluation times per snapshot (uniform grid over the window, as in PFM_).

  • t_eval (array - like or None, default: None ) –

    Explicit evaluation times (e.g. interval midpoints); overrides fac.

  • ridge (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Ridge penalty on the drift matrix (time-averaged loss).

  • n_rounds –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • anderson –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • safeguard –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • tol –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • push_steps –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • history –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

  • verbose –

    Iteration settings, as in PFM_LINEAR_.

Returns:

  • ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim) –

    Limit of the fitted drift matrix.

docs.title: random_ou(ndim, rng, skew_scale=0.5)
docs.text:
Random stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with symmetric and skew-symmetric parts.

The drift matrix is B = S + A, with S = Q diag(lambda) Q^T (Q Haar-random orthogonal, lambda_i ~ U[0.1, 2], so B is stable) and A = skew_scale (G - G^T) / 2 (G_ij ~ N(0, 1)). The diffusion is D = 0.5 I. The initial law is far from stationarity: m0 ~ N(0, 9 I) and S0 = R diag(0.1 logspace(-1, 0, ndim)) R^T (R Haar-random).

Parameters:

  • ndim (int) –

    State dimension.

  • rng (Generator) –

    Random generator.

  • skew_scale (float, default: 0.5 ) –

    Scale of the skew-symmetric part; 0 gives a gradient (symmetric) drift.

Returns:

  • B ( ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim) ) –

    Drift matrix, dx = -B x dt + sqrt(2 D) dW.

  • D ( ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim) ) –

    Diffusion matrix.

  • m0 ( ndarray of shape (ndim,) ) –

    Initial mean.

  • S0 ( ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim) ) –

    Initial covariance.

docs.title: sample_ornstein_uhlenbeck(B, D, m0, S0, times, nsamples, rng)
docs.text:
Sample independent snapshots of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, exactly.

Each snapshot is drawn from the exact Gaussian law at its time (:func:ou_moments), independently of the others, in the order of times.

Parameters:

  • B (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Drift and diffusion matrices.

  • D (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Drift and diffusion matrices.

  • m0 (ndarray of shape (ndim,)) –

    Initial mean.

  • S0 (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Initial covariance.

  • times (array-like of shape (K,)) –

    Snapshot times.

  • nsamples (int) –

    Number of cells per snapshot.

  • rng (Generator) –

    Random generator.

Returns:

  • samples ( list of length K ) –

    samples[k] is an ndarray of shape (nsamples, ndim).

  • times ( ndarray of shape (K,) ) –

    Snapshot times.

docs.title: simulate_ornstein_uhlenbeck(Om, D, m0, S0, nsamples, ndim, Dt, K, dt=0.006)
docs.text:
Simulate snapshots from a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process.

Legacy: kept for backward compatibility with existing tests and examples. New code should use :func:sample_ornstein_uhlenbeck, which samples the exact Gaussian laws (no time-discretization error) for any initial covariance.

Parameters:

  • Om (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Drift matrix.

  • D (ndarray of shape (ndim, ndim)) –

    Diffusion matrix.

  • m0 (ndarray of shape (ndim,)) –

    Mean of the initial Gaussian distribution.

  • S0 (float) –

    Isotropic variance factor for the initial covariance S0 * I.

  • nsamples (int) –

    Number of particles sampled at each snapshot time.

  • ndim (int) –

    State dimension.

  • Dt (float) –

    Snapshot interval in simulation time.

  • K (int) –

    Number of snapshots.

  • dt (float, default: 0.006 ) –

    Euler-Maruyama integration step.

Returns:

  • samples ( list of length K ) –

    samples[k] is an ndarray of shape (nsamples, ndim).

  • tt ( ndarray of shape (K,) ) –

    Snapshot times.

docs.title: simulate_toggle_switch(model_params, vol, gr, nsamples, ndim, Dt, K, dt=0.01)
docs.text:
Simulate snapshots from stochastic toggle-switch dynamics.

Parameters:

  • model_params (array-like of shape (7,)) –

    Toggle-switch parameters [a1, a2, b1, b2, k1, k2, n].

  • vol (float) –

    System volume scaling the stochastic term.

  • gr (float) –

    Growth-rate scale. Growth is active only when gr > 0.

  • nsamples (int) –

    Number of particles sampled at the initial time.

  • ndim (int) –

    State dimension.

  • Dt (float) –

    Snapshot interval in simulation time.

  • K (int) –

    Number of snapshots.

  • dt (float, default: 0.01 ) –

    Euler-Maruyama integration step.

Returns:

  • samples_full ( list of length K ) –

    samples_full[k] is an ndarray of shape (n_k, ndim), where n_k can increase across snapshots when growth is active.

  • tt ( ndarray of shape (K,) ) –

    Snapshot times.
